greeting: Ataniup Quviasuktitilluta, Atanirmik Piluta. Ateqarfik Ataniup Atianik, Irniup, Anersaap Illup. Amen.
penitential: Atani, nalligiagut. Christ, nalligiagut. Atani, nalligiagut.
homily:
It is a quiet, steady kind of darkness when you sit by a window and watch the night settle over the rooftops. You can see the faint blinking lights of an aircraft high above, tracking its silent line across the deep indigo sky, carrying people toward somewhere they long to be. We have all stood there at some hour, watching things move away from us into the distance, wondering how something so vast can hold so much emptiness. Saint Luke tells us today of Jesus climbing the mountain alone, spending the entire night in the quiet dark talking to the Father before the morning broke. He did not rush the night. He stayed in the silence under the stars, letting the weight of what was coming rest upon His shoulders, choosing twelve men not because they were polished or finished, but simply because He wanted them near. Simon, Andrew, James, John, and the others—ordinary men pulled from their nets and tax booths, made stones for a building that had not yet risen.

Saint Paul writes to the Ephesians about this very building, telling us that we are no longer strangers and sojourners, but fellow citizens with the holy ones, 'built upon the foundation of the Apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the capstone.' A capstone is the final, locking stone at the very top of an arch. Without it, the walls lean outward and the whole structure falls into the dust. With it, every heavy block beneath it finds its balance and holds firm against the wind. Christ is that stone for us today. He is the weight that keeps the roof over our heads when the storms come howling across the open plains.

We know what those storms look like, don't we? Alan and Thao, I know how the silence feels in the morning when the sun hits the floorboards and the weight of four months settles over your chest all over again. Ryan, I know how it is to look across the room and miss your brother, to remember the snowy days wrapped in heavy coats and the sound of laughter in the cold air. The grief does not ask for permission when it arrives; it just walks in and sits by your chair. You try to keep busy, you try to move through the day, but then a memory catches you by the throat—a pair of shoes left by the door, a song on the radio, or the thought of a boy who loved airplanes so much he joked about starting 'con chim airlines' with a bright, infectious giggle. It hurts because you loved deeply. There is no shortcut around that ache. If the pain is immense, it is only because the love was just as large.

And sometimes, in the quietest hours of the night, the mind starts turning over stones it has no business touching. You wonder if you missed a sign. You replay every day, every moment, every breath, whispering to yourselves that you should have seen something sooner, done something differently. Let me lift that heavy stone from your heart right now, because God is not keeping a ledger of your perceived failings. Illness is never a punishment, and it is never the fault of those who loved and cared for the one who suffered. Some sorrows in this life come completely beyond human control, like weather rolling in across the sea from a place we cannot see. No watchfulness could have stopped it, no amount of care could have held back the tide. You did not fail Benjamin. You loved him with every breath you had, right to the very end, and he knew it. He knew he was adored by the best dad and the best mom a boy could ever ask for.

Think of the way Benjamin lived his fifteen years. He was a boy whose mind reached out toward the stars, coding games on GitHub, talking cloud infrastructure and AI with the maturity of a man twice his age, yet keeping that gentle, unassuming soul. Remember the sweet purity of his heart—like the time when, unprompted and completely sincere, he told his parents he was willing to give up his entire piggy bank to help his uncle through a hard time. He didn't need to break the porcelain open or empty the coins; the beauty was simply in the offer. It was a boy willing to hand over everything he possessed for someone else. That is the kind of heart Christ builds His church upon. That is the kind of love that does not die when the breath leaves the body.

Jesus spent the night on the mountain so He could face the dawn. And when the dawn came, He called His friends by name. Simon, Peter, Jude, and the rest—they were flawed, they were fragile, and yet they became the foundation. Benjamin is not a stranger to that household of God today. He is a fellow citizen with the holy ones, resting in the light of the capstone who holds the universe together. When your heart feels squeezed by the silence, remember that love is not bounded by the grave. When you look up and see a commercial jet climbing through the clouds, let it remind you that Ben’s spirit is free, soaring in a peace this world cannot give.

Take this one small thing with you out the door today: whenever a heavy wave of grief hits you, stop for three seconds, take a slow breath, and say his name out loud. Let it be a prayer of thanksgiving that he was yours, and you were his. God does not ask you to stop hurting; He only asks you to let Him carry it with you. You are held, you are seen, and you are never alone. May the peace of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, guard your hearts and minds today and forever. Amen.

closing: Ataniup asannininga ilissik piurquvuq, aniguqtilaaqtut nuannaartuq. Amen.
standing_petitions: Benjamin, taanna qaujimajavut tallimat pivalliajut, nuannaartuq, qajangnartuq, pinniqtuq. Taanna nalligivikluq, nalligikpatiklu qitiqquqsimajuq.

day: Feast of Saints Simon and Jude, Apostles

pet_prayers.text: Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.
